# Layouts

> Arrange the active tab's panes in a row, column, or grid, keep one pane on the left, and balance pane sizes with Paneflow's layout shortcuts.

Canonical: https://paneflow.dev/docs/layouts

<!-- Auto-generated mirror of paneflow.dev - do not edit by hand.
     Source of truth: the paneflow.dev docs. Regenerated by
     scripts/sync-public-docs.ts in the site repo. -->

Paneflow's four layout presets rearrange the panes already open in the
**active tab**. Use them to compare agent output, read wide logs, or keep
one session beside several others. Running commands continue in their panes.

## Choose and apply a layout

From a pane in the tab, press one of the shortcuts below. Use `Cmd` on
macOS and `Ctrl` on Linux and Windows. You can also open the command palette
with `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P`, select **Pane layout**, and choose a preset.

The names below match the command palette.

| Preset | Shortcut | Arrangement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Even horizontal** | `Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+1` | One row of panes with equal widths. |
| **Even vertical** | `Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+2` | One column of panes with equal heights. |
| **Main vertical** | `Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+3` | The focused pane on the left, with the others stacked on the right. Each side takes half the width. |
| **Tiled** | `Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+4` | A grid whose rows and columns depend on the number of panes. |

- Choose **Even horizontal** to compare short outputs on a wide screen.
- Choose **Even vertical** when logs or commands need the full tab width.
- Choose **Main vertical** to follow one agent beside tests or other sessions.
  Focus the pane you want on the left before applying the preset.
- Choose **Tiled** to watch several sessions without making one the main view.

**Main vertical** keeps focus on the pane you selected. The other presets
move focus to the first pane in the new layout. With only one pane, applying
a preset leaves its arrangement unchanged.

## Balance sizes without rearranging panes

Press `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+=` to run `split_equalize`. It balances the space
between panes within each existing split and keeps them in their current
arrangement.

Use this after resizing panes if you want to keep the same rows and columns.
A layout preset replaces the arrangement and its size proportions instead.

## Keep working in the same sessions

Applying a preset reuses the existing panes. It keeps their shells, running
commands, terminal history, and working directories. A build or agent task
continues after its pane moves. Other tabs keep their layouts.

Keeping sessions running when you quit Paneflow is a separate choice. Select
**Keep sessions running** on quit, then reopen the app to reconnect. The
session host and machine must remain running. See the
[guide to terminal sessions](/docs/features) for stopping, reopening, and
restarting sessions.

## Configure layouts and shortcuts

To change a shortcut, bind its action name under `shortcuts` in
`paneflow.json`. Workspace templates and `paneflow up` use the preset values
in the last column instead.

| Preset | Shortcut action | Preset value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Even horizontal | `layout_even_horizontal` | `even_h` |
| Even vertical | `layout_even_vertical` | `even_v` |
| Main vertical | `layout_main_vertical` | `main_vertical` |
| Tiled | `layout_tiled` | `tiled` |

In a workspace template, set `commands[].workspace.layout_preset`.
In a `paneflow up` file, set `layout`. Choosing a preset for a new workspace
sets its initial arrangement; applying a shortcut rearranges an existing tab.

Follow the [shortcut customization guide](/docs/keybindings) to remap keys,
the [workspace template reference](/docs/configuration/schema) to configure
reusable workspaces, or the [CLI automation guide](/docs/scripting) to open
workspaces from files.
